Listen to this article Share Troops of Operation Hadin Kai have neutralised four senior leaders of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), including two Arab fighters, a prominent commander and several other terrorists during a military engagement in Kukawa Local Government Area of Borno State. The Nigerian Army said the operation was conducted on Sunday, by combined troops of the Joint Task Force deployed to Kukawa following a massive attack by ISWAP terrorists on their locations. The troops, according to the Army, deployed both ground and air assets from the Air Component of Operation Hadin Kai to repel the attack and neutralise the terrorists. Mohammed Goni, acting Military Information Officer, Northeast Joint Task Force, Operation Hadin Kai, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, describing the engagement as a significant setback for the leadership and operational capacity of the terrorist group. He said the four high-ranking terrorists neutralised included Abu Hajara, a prominent member of ISWAP’s Shura Council, and Abul Walid, a senior commander and close associate of Ba Shuwa, the overall Wali of ISWAP. The other two were described as high-ranking Arab fighters. Read also: UK opens door to slavery apology but rules out financial reparations According to Army, the troops also recovered scores of arms, ammunition and communication devices following the engagement. “Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), have dealt a significant blow to the leadership and operational capability of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), neutralising several terrorists during an engagement in Kukawa, Borno State, on 31 October 2026,” the statement said. It said the successful operation demonstrated the combat readiness, vigilance and superior firepower of troops in sustaining pressure on terrorist groups operating across the theatre. “The successful engagement further demonstrates the combat readiness, vigilance and superior firepower of Operation Hadin Kai troops in sustaining pressure on terrorist elements across the theatre,” Army stated. The attack on the troops’ location in Kukawa came barely three days after a military operation in Buni Yadi, where 55 terrorists were neutralised, including key commanders Ali Mandara Abba Gajiri, also known as Munzir; Habu Ikkima Nakif Yana Faruk; and Commander Gogore. The statement said the Theatre Command had reaffirmed its commitment to protecting law-abiding citizens and sustaining military operations aimed at eliminating terrorist groups and destroying their camps across the region.
